The logo: the words on one wave with the cards

Holger, 28 Sep, with a sketch: the wavy one is better, but can it feel even more like a wave; if you drew a helping line through the cards and the text, would that help it feel more connected, part of the same wave? So: the two lines on one sine that leaves the front card’s corner at the card’s own lean and runs back along its top edge, inside a band as tall as the card, five ways: the trough at the middle, the helping lines drawn, the trough later, a deeper wave, the trough earlier. N2 is kept as it was. Then, at his next word, the apps’ characters as the mark: the queen of Pinochle, the jack of Euchre, the queen of Gin Rummy, the king of Rummy and the joker of Canasta, each alone without the cards, read off its Photoshop layer with no shadow, its bottom finished with rounded corners and the black line, facing away from the words, at 1.32 times the fan’s height beside the words of the logo the site uses now, at their size today. The keepers stay as they are. On 29 Sep Holger added a logo of his own, logo-test-transprent.png, drawn as one picture in row Q1 at the bar’s 32px, and his third file, the words a weight lighter and the cards’ outline heavier, as Q2 (it replaced his second, which had only the lighter words); then N2 with World of out to the G of Games, R1 to R3, and R2 in the mockup’s six favourite title faces, S1 to S6; the same in all 38 faces of that menu, mixed case and in capitals, and then in 27 sans faces, is the sheet logo-faces.html. Every row has a number and a name (say “O3”). Each row: the logo at 64px, then the site’s bar at a desktop width with the logo 32px tall, and a phone with it 24px tall; the figure rows stand at the height that keeps today’s words at today’s size, and the tall switch grows every logo to 36px (27 on the phone).

O The words on one wave with the cards

Holger, with a sketch of two red lines: the wavy one is better, but can it feel even more like a wave; if you drew a helping line through the cards and the text, would that make it feel more connected, part of the same wave? So: a sine leaves the front card’s top-right corner at the card’s own lean, dips to a trough under the words and rises again, and to the left of the corner it runs back along the card’s top edge. Both lines are parallel offsets of that one curve, inside a band as tall as the card, so the band’s top edge is the card’s top edge carried on and its bottom edge the card’s bottom edge carried on. Nothing else changes from N2: the size, the weight, the air between the lines, the starts, the gap to the card. One row draws the helping lines.

O1

One wave

The words on the wave that leaves the card’s corner at the card’s lean, the trough at the middle of the words

The band’s top edge is the front card’s top edge carried on as a sine; World of hangs under it and Card Games sits over the bottom edge, the card’s bottom edge carried on. The wave leaves the corner at ten degrees, dips 18 of the fan’s 100 by the middle of the words, and rises at ten degrees again by their end.

P The apps’ characters as the mark, with today’s logotype

Holger: the character alone, no cards; the bottom with the same black line as the rest of the character; every character facing away from the words; and the character about 30% bigger against the words, then 15% bigger again, then 10% more, then 20% smaller, with the words at the size they have today. So the queen of Pinochle, the jack of Euchre, the queen of Gin Rummy, the king of Rummy and the joker of Canasta each stand in the fan’s place at 1.32 times the fan’s height, their right edge where the fan’s box ended, with today’s outlined Bariol Bold words at today’s size and distance, centred on the mark; these rows are drawn and barred at the height that keeps the words at today’s size, so the logo stands taller than today’s 32px on the bar. Each character is read off its own layer in the app icon’s Photoshop source with psd-tools, without the card layers and without the group’s drop shadow; its white sticker outline is a stroke on its own group and comes with it. The illustrator’s straight cut at the bottom is finished with rounded corners at 7% of the height, the black line at the thickness of the character’s own line art, and the white outline outside it, so the bottom edge reads like every other edge. The jack and the joker face the words as drawn and are mirrored; the king and the two queens face away as drawn.

Q Holger’s test logo, as one picture

Holger, 29 Sep: a new logo, logo-test-transprent.png in his Downloads, to add to the test. It is drawn here as one picture, the fan and the words together, nothing redrawn: scaled so its fan stands at the height the lab’s fans do, and barred at the bar’s 32px like every row but the figure rows. In it four aces of hearts fan out under a dark outline, and World of over Card Games stand to the right in a heavy rounded serif, both lines on a gentle bowl that falls from the front card and rises again, the block reaching a little below the fan. Q2 is his third file, in place of the second: the words a weight lighter, and the cards’ outline heavier and rounder.
